files.why: Add framework-free BillingPeriod entity (id, name, start, end) and a BillingPeriodSummary read model carrying precomputed totals/counts so consumers never rerun rules.
Add pure rules to select invoices/appointments falling in a period's date range and fold their invoiceTotalMinor into per-period totals, plus a summarizePeriod projection.
Add billingPeriodDtoSchema (server shape: snake_case id/name/start_date/end_date) so the period fetch is validated like every other DTO.
Add toBillingPeriod mapping DTO ISO dates -> core Date entity, keeping DTOs from leaking upward.
Add fetchBillingPeriods / fetchBillingPeriodById that compose invoices-in-range with scheduling appointment summaries and emit the totalled read model.
Seed a few billing periods and add MSW handlers for /api/billing-periods so the feature has data under the mocked API.
Append /billing-periods and /billing-periods/:id route records to the existing billingRoutes array (slice owns its paths; app router only concatenates).
UI state hook loading the list of periods with their totals, mirroring useInvoiceList's shape.
Detail hook that joins a period's invoices with scheduling appointments via the @slices/scheduling public alias (the canonical cross-slice pattern).
List view of periods (name, range, total) using shared Card/Table primitives.
Detail view rendering a period's grouped appointments, invoices, and totals.
Add fetchAppointmentsInRange(start,end) -> AppointmentSummary[]; existing public queries are by-client/by-ids/upcoming only, none give 'appointments that happened in a range'.
Expose the new range query on scheduling's public surface so billing can consume it without a deep import.
Cover the new period selection/total rules with the existing pure-core test style.
Cover toBillingPeriod DTO<->core date mapping alongside the existing mapper tests.

uncertain: Whether billing/index.ts needs new public exports. Periods are viewed inside billing's own routes (already re-exported via billingRoutes), so no new export is strictly required; it only changes if the app-level ClientOverviewView (or another slice) must show period totals, in which case export BillingPeriodSummary + fetchBillingPeriods there.

Whether a 'billing period' belongs inside the billing slice or is its own slice. I placed it in billing because it's a finance/pricing concept keyed on invoices and 'billing period' is a billing domain noun; but it also spans scheduling, so an architecture reviewer might argue for a third slice (which would mean adding it to `slices` in architecture.config.ts and standing up the full 5-entry folder).

Where the range predicate for 'appointments that happened in the period' lives. I put the filter in scheduling/data/queries.ts, but if the team wants it as a reusable pure rule it could instead be an `occursWithin` predicate in scheduling/core/rules.ts (which would also add a scheduling.core.test.ts change).

Whether creating/naming periods is in scope. If finance CREATES periods (the word 'named' suggests it), I'd also modify billing/data/mutations.ts (+ a POST /api/billing-periods mock handler) and add toBillingPeriodDto in mappers.ts — omitted above because the request reads as reporting/grouping.

Whether a 'named date range' picker is needed for creating periods. Per README worked example 3 a generic date-range picker is a shared/ui primitive, but rule 7 says duplicate in billing/ui until the 3rd same-reason use — so I would NOT create shared/ui yet.
Whether the period totals card warrants its own ui/components/*.vue (e.g. PeriodTotals) or should stay inline in the detail view; I left it inline to avoid a premature component.
questions: Is this read-only reporting (view periods + totals) or do finance users create/edit/name periods themselves? That decides whether mutations + POST handlers are in scope.
How is a period defined — arbitrary user-chosen date ranges, or fixed recurring cycles (monthly/quarterly) generated by rule? This affects whether we store period records or derive them.

Which totals does finance actually want per period: sum of invoice totals only, or also subtotal/tax breakdowns, invoice count, appointment count, per-currency splits? Invoices carry a currency field, so are periods single-currency or must totals be grouped by currency?

What is 'raised for them' precisely — which invoice date decides membership (issueDate vs dueDate), and which appointment timestamp counts as 'happened in' (start vs end)? And how do statuses (draft/void invoices, cancelled appointments) affect the totals?

Should periods scope to a single client or aggregate across all clients? The existing read models (fetchUnpaidInvoiceSummaries, fetchUpcomingAppointments) are client-scoped, whereas a finance-wide billing period likely is not.
Does a new server API for periods exist (shape/fields), or am I inventing the DTO for the mock only? Confirming the real endpoint contract avoids guessing snake_case field names.
Should the client overview or any existing surface link to periods, or is this a standalone /billing-periods area?
